title: Unit 01 archival, documentary and literary synthesis mission

questions.prompt: Many Voices migration exhibit: choose a defensible description of original council minutes concerning a fictional relocation.
choices: Un procès-verbal contemporain, à interpréter dans son contexte institutionnel.
Un témoignage représentant nécessairement tous les habitants.
Une preuve que toute décision fut acceptée.
questions.explanation: Contemporaneous minutes are primary institutional evidence with perspective limits.

questions.prompt: Migration-memory synthesis: distinguish a survivor's memoir of displacement from a novel inspired by migration.
choices: Les deux genres offrent nécessairement des citations directes des mêmes événements.
Un roman est toujours un registre administratif.
Un mémoire témoigne d'un vécu revendiqué; un roman peut inventer des scènes.
questions.explanation: A memoir claims personal recollection while fiction can reconstruct imagined scenes.

questions.prompt: Fictional family migration records: choose a careful hypothetical past inference about what a surviving archive might have shown.
choices: Les archives imaginaires prouvent ce qui s'est passé.
Si les archives avaient survécu, nous aurions pu comparer les versions.
Si les archives survivront, nous aurions comparé hier.
questions.explanation: A plus-que-parfait condition and past conditional denote an unreal past.

questions.prompt: Identity and migration documentary: which French sentence transparently acknowledges a translation that changes a political nuance?
choices: La traduction atténue une nuance du terme original, ce qui mérite une note.
La traduction privilégie une expression plus fluide, sans indiquer au lecteur la modification du sens.
La traduction propose une reformulation qui peut masquer l'origine du terme si aucune note n'est ajoutée.
questions.explanation: The keyed formulation directly identifies the altered political nuance and requests disclosure; the alternatives either omit disclosure or leave the specific shift unidentified.

questions.prompt: Fictional relocation chronicles disagree: which expression attributes the disputed report rather than endorsing it?
choices: Il est incontestable que la réunion fut annulée sans source.
La chronique représente automatiquement chaque témoin.
Selon cette chronique tardive, la réunion aurait été annulée.
questions.explanation: Selon and the reporting conditional signal attribution and uncertainty.

questions.prompt: A migrant family's departure is staged in a documentary. Which French description distinguishes re-enactment from original footage?
choices: Une preuve audiovisuelle originale créée après les faits.
Une scène reconstituée, distincte des archives d'époque.
Une prise de vue directe d'un événement non filmé.
questions.explanation: Reconstruction must be distinguished from contemporaneous documentary footage.

questions.prompt: Migration oral-history exhibit: which formulation respects one community interview without treating it as everyone's experience?
choices: Ce témoignage expose une expérience, sans épuiser les perspectives du groupe.
Ce témoignage peut éclairer la communauté si ses propos sont présentés comme représentatifs de tous.
Ce témoignage est une source importante; ses conclusions remplacent les récits contradictoires.
questions.explanation: The best response values one witness while marking the limits of representativeness; neither group generalization nor dismissal of other accounts is justified.

questions.prompt: Editing a translated migrant testimony for an exhibit: which French practice clearly identifies omitted source text?
choices: Les omissions sont cachées pour faciliter une conclusion.
Des paroles inexistantes sont ajoutées entre guillemets.
Les coupes sont signalées et les passages omis restent consultables.
questions.explanation: Transparent omissions preserve a clear boundary between original and edited text.

questions.prompt: Migration and belonging exhibit: choose a balanced thesis contrasting official archives and personal poetic memory.
choices: Le poème rend toute archive nécessairement fausse.
L'archive précise les décisions, tandis que le poème révèle une mémoire subjective.
Les deux sources prouvent le même vécu de chaque participant.
questions.explanation: Different genres can convey institutional evidence and subjective memory.

questions.prompt: Read: « La lettre date de 1912, mais sa traduction a été publiée en 1970 ». Which date belongs to the source letter?
choices: Neither date is given.
questions.explanation: The letter's creation year is distinguished from the later translation.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le récit utilise 'nous', sans préciser le groupe désigné ». What is unclear?
choices: Whether French permits plural pronouns.
The document's punctuation length.
Whose collective perspective the author claims.
questions.explanation: Unspecified nous leaves collective representation ambiguous.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le film fait entendre une voix d'acteur sur une lettre d'époque ». What is mediated?
choices: The recording must be a voice from the event.
The historic letter is performed by a later actor.
The actor necessarily wrote the original letter.
questions.explanation: A later performance is not the original speaker's sound.

questions.prompt: Read: « Des registres indiquent des départs, non leurs causes individuelles ». What cannot be inferred directly?
choices: Why each person departed.
Whether departures were recorded.
That records had administrative uses.
questions.explanation: Departure counts alone do not establish personal motives.

questions.prompt: Read: « L'éditorial affirme que la réforme était juste, mais la correspondance révèle des protestations ». What is shown?
choices: Everyone endorsed the reform.
No editorial opinion was offered.
A favorable argument and evidence of dissent coexist.
questions.explanation: A stated editorial position does not erase documented dissent.

questions.prompt: Read: « Si la réunion avait été publique, d'autres voix auraient été entendues ». What sort of claim is this?
choices: A verified audio transcript of that meeting.
A counterfactual about an unobserved alternative.
A certified list of actual speakers.
questions.explanation: The conditional past describes an alternative, not a witnessed event.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le roman situe la scène dans une ville réelle, mais invente le dialogue ». What is documented?
choices: The place may be real; dialogue remains fictional.
Every conversation in the novel is primary testimony.
The city is fictional by necessity.
questions.explanation: A real setting does not convert invented dialogue into historic evidence.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le sous-titre gomme l'emploi d'un dialecte régional ». What is potentially lost?
choices: The film's physical running time.
The date of every filmed scene.
A meaningful signal of speaker identity and register.
questions.explanation: Erasing a regional variety can remove sociolinguistic context.

questions.prompt: Read: « Une photo a été recadrée sans mention de son contexte initial ». What question follows?
choices: Whether framing can never affect interpretation.
What people or details may be excluded by the crop?
Whether the photograph was produced without light.
questions.explanation: Cropping may alter what a viewer understands about the original scene.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: compare a survivor's recollection with an official report. What should the analysis preserve?
choices: Distinct perspectives, dates and reasons for each document's creation.
An assumption that official sources automatically override all testimony.
A merged quotation never spoken by either source.
questions.explanation: Comparison must maintain provenance and perspective rather than fabricate agreement.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: a museum label calls a reconstruction an original photograph. What correction is essential?
choices: Keep the false caption to make the exhibit immersive.
Remove the image date to avoid scrutiny.
Identify the image as a later reconstruction and cite its basis.
questions.explanation: The exhibit must distinguish reconstruction from primary photographic evidence.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: two translations render « mémoire » differently. What should be compared?
choices: Which translator has the most prestigious surname.
Original passage, genre, register and intended meaning.
Only which translation is shorter.
questions.explanation: Mémoire varies with context, so comparison needs original-language evidence.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: an archive omits voices of displaced people. Which response is ethical?
choices: Name the gap and seek relevant community-held sources.
Invent testimonies to balance the archive.
Conclude that displaced people left no perspectives.
questions.explanation: Documenting gaps and seeking additional sources avoids fabrication.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: an author claims a past treaty would certainly have prevented conflict. What is a careful revision?
choices: Le traité aurait éliminé toute violence sans autre preuve.
Une hypothèse est une observation directe.
Le traité aurait peut-être réduit le risque, mais le scénario reste hypothétique.
questions.explanation: Maybe and an explicit counterfactual qualifier prevent false certainty.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: a film combines archival sound with staged images. How should you annotate it?
choices: Présenter le montage comme un document audiovisuel non édité.
Distinguer l'enregistrement d'époque des images reconstituées.
Attribuer chaque image mise en scène à une caméra d'époque.
questions.explanation: The provenance of audio and constructed images must remain distinct.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: several sources use a historical label now considered derogatory. What should your report do?
choices: Contextualize limited quotations and prefer respectful present-day description.
Repeat the label as neutral in every heading.
Erase the term without explaining its historical presence.
questions.explanation: Historical harmful language can be documented without endorsing its viewpoint.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: an interview's French transcription silently removes hesitations. What should be recorded?
choices: That the original speaker never hesitated.
That the edited transcript must be identical to the recording.
The editorial normalization and its possible effect on meaning.
questions.explanation: Transparency about editing helps readers evaluate spoken testimony.

questions.prompt: Synthesis: finish an exhibit comparison with an evidence-aware conclusion.
choices: Une œuvre choisie remplace toutes les sources contradictoires.
Ces œuvres éclairent des aspects différents de l'événement; aucune ne résume seule toutes les expériences.
Les archives, films et poèmes ont toujours une portée probante identique.
questions.explanation: A good synthesis recognizes genre differences and limits of representation.
